hints: Start by thinking about what is actually in the beaker after the carbonates dissolve in nitric acid.
Remember your solubility rules, all nitrates are soluble, most chlorides are soluble, but barium sulfate is famously insoluble.
Look for the reagent that will make only one of the two metal ions form a solid, so you can filter it off and leave the other in solution.
walkthrough:
**What is in solution first?**

Both carbonates react with nitric acid to give soluble nitrates, water and carbon dioxide. So you now have a mixture of aqueous ions.

$$\text{MgCO}_3 + 2\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Mg(NO}_3)_2(aq) + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{BaCO}_3 + 2\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Ba(NO}_3)_2(aq) + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**What do we need for separation?**

To separate $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ by filtration, we need to add an anion that gives a precipitate with one ion but stays in solution with the other. This is all about solubility differences.

**Test chloride vs sulfate**

All Group 2 chlorides are soluble, so adding $\text{HCl}$ gives $\text{MgCl}_2(aq)$ and $\text{BaCl}_2(aq)$ with no solid to filter. For sulfates, solubility drops down the group, $\text{MgSO}_4$ is soluble but $\text{BaSO}_4$ is insoluble.

$$\text{Ba}^{2+}(aq) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4(s)$$

**Conclude the method**

Add dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(aq)$. White solid $\text{BaSO}_4$ precipitates and is filtered off as the separate barium compound. The filtrate still contains soluble $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, as $\text{MgSO}_4$ or $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$, as the separate magnesium compound.

options.A: Incorrect. Barium chloride is soluble in water, so no solid barium chloride would form. Adding HCl just leaves both $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ in solution as chlorides, with no separation.
options.B: Incorrect. Magnesium chloride is very soluble, so nothing would precipitate to filter off. This option confuses the solubility rules, both chlorides stay dissolved.
options.C: Correct. Barium sulfate is insoluble while magnesium sulfate is soluble. Adding $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ precipitates $\text{BaSO}_4(s)$ which can be filtered off, leaving the magnesium compound in the filtrate. This gives a clean separation.
options.D: Incorrect. It gets the reagent right but the solid wrong. Magnesium sulfate is soluble, so it stays in the filtrate. The solid filtered off is barium sulfate, not magnesium sulfate.
